items.followUp: Define cathode rays and state any three of their properties.

rubric.why: The answer must identify canal rays as positively charged particles and connect their name to their passage through the perforated cathode.
rubric.description: Definition and passage through the cathode
rubric.how: Award 2 marks when both the positive charge and passage through holes or canals in a perforated cathode are stated.

rubric.why: Canal rays travel along straight paths.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that canal rays travel in straight lines.

rubric.why: This point covers two properties: deflection by fields and dependence of the particles' properties on the gas in the tube.
rubric.description: Deflection by fields and dependence on the gas
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deflection by an electric or magnetic field and 1 mark for stating that their nature or properties depend on the gas.

modelAnswer: Canal rays are streams of positively charged particles (positive ions) produced in a gas-discharge tube.
They pass through holes or canals in a perforated cathode.
They are deflected by electric and magnetic fields; in an electric field, they bend toward the negative plate.
Their nature and properties depend on the gas present in the tube.

items.followUp: Compare the reactions of alkali metals and alkaline earth metals with oxygen, halogens and hydrogen.

rubric.why: Alkali metals react more vigorously with water than alkaline earth metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct comparison of their reactions with water, including the greater vigour of alkali metals.

rubric.why: Alkali metals can form oxides, peroxides or superoxides, whereas alkaline earth metals generally form oxides.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly distinguishing the oxygen compounds formed by the two groups.

rubric.why: Alkali metals form monovalent halides (MX), while alkaline earth metals form divalent halides (MX₂).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing the halides formed, such as MX and MX₂.

rubric.why: Alkali metals form monovalent hydrides (MH), while alkaline earth metals form divalent hydrides (MH₂).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing the hydrides formed, such as MH and MH₂.

modelAnswer: With water: Alkali metals react vigorously to form hydroxides and hydrogen; alkaline earth metals react less vigorously. Beryllium does not react with water, while magnesium reacts with hot water or steam.
With oxygen: Alkali metals may form oxides, peroxides or superoxides; alkaline earth metals generally form oxides.
With halogens: Alkali metals form monovalent halides of formula MX, while alkaline earth metals form divalent halides of formula MX₂.
With hydrogen: Alkali metals form monovalent hydrides of formula MH, while alkaline earth metals form divalent hydrides of formula MH₂.
